evals.prompt: Build a tiny Bun CLI that uses @valentinkolb/nessi/ai with OpenRouter to summarize text passed as a command-line argument. It should print streamed text as it arrives and read OPENROUTER_API_KEY from the environment.
evals.expected_output: A concise Bun/TypeScript CLI using openrouter(model, options), provider.stream(), block_start/block_delta text handling, issue/usage event handling, and no browser-exposed secrets.

evals.prompt: I want a provider switcher for my Node service: use local Ollama in development and OpenAI in production. Show the @valentinkolb/nessi/ai code and keep the rest of the app independent from the provider choice.
evals.expected_output: A provider factory returning the shared Provider interface, using ollama(model, options) and openai(model, options), plus an example complete() call.

evals.prompt: Show me how to do tool calling with @valentinkolb/nessi/ai only. I have a search_docs function and want the model to request it, then send the tool result back for a final answer.
evals.expected_output: A consumer-side tool-call loop using tools inputSchema, complete(), assistant tool_call block extraction, tool_result messages, and a follow-up complete() call. It should mention that @valentinkolb/nessi/ai does not execute tools automatically.

evals.prompt: Build a tiny Bun agent with @valentinkolb/nessi that stores history in memory, uses OpenRouter, defines one server-side search_docs tool with zod, and streams text to stdout.
evals.expected_output: A concise agent-loop example importing nessi, defineTool, and memoryStore from @valentinkolb/nessi, importing openrouter from @valentinkolb/nessi/ai, defining a zod-backed server tool, passing store: memoryStore() and tools to nessi(), and iterating loop events for block_start/block_delta text handling, issue handling, and loop_end.aggregate/loopId handling.

evals.prompt: I need a typed task extractor with @valentinkolb/nessi. It should return a validated Zod object, accept an image input, and may call one server-side lookup tool before returning.
evals.expected_output: A root nessi.structured() example importing nessi and defineTool from @valentinkolb/nessi, importing a provider from @valentinkolb/nessi/ai, defining a Zod output schema, passing string or multimodal content parts as input, optionally passing only server tools, and reading result.output plus result.structuredMeta/result.aggregate. It should not use provider.complete() for the high-level typed task unless explicitly discussing low-level responseFormat.

evals.prompt: My Nessi loop runs in a background worker, but steering instructions arrive through separate HTTP requests and are stored in my database. Show how the worker can pick them up without continuously polling while the provider or tools are running. I also need local loop.steer() to keep working and want to show applied steering in the UI.
evals.expected_output: A root nessi() example using the optional steering callback to return one pending message, an ordered array, or undefined from application-owned persistence, while retaining loop.steer(). It should handle steer_applied as the shared UI confirmation, explain that Nessi checks only at safe loop boundaries including before provider calls and normal completion, and leave claiming, persistence, and delivery guarantees to the application.
